display: Austin live sound engineer with 20 years in club rooms, now designing full-sounding mixes at low volume.

signals.text: I want to put on a quiet show for people who can't handle loud rooms: kids, people with sensory sensitivities, older folks. I don't know who would host it or where.
I've spent about a year in my garage mixing under 70 dB, and I'd like someone to actually want this work.
I'm keeping notes on per-instrument EQ curves at low SPL and would like to compare them with other engineers or turn them into something shareable.
I'm looking for a venue, community space or organizer willing to try a sub-70 dB, no-strobe event with a quiet room.
I'm recording a local acoustic trio in November and want to find more acoustic players willing to play soft.
I read about sensory-friendly concerts for kids and realized I'd been doing the technical side already, but nobody had asked for it.
I'm stuck mid-rebuild on a 1974 Honda CB550 (carburettor kit, wiring harness, tank paint) and could use a hand from someone who knows vintage Hondas.
I'm worried that my hearing may limit how long I can keep working loud rooms, and I'm starting to think about what comes next.
Money is tight right now, so small paid jobs on weekday mornings would help.
A family member just moved into assisted living and misses her radio and garden. I'm looking for ways to make that place feel less silent for her.
I'm coaching an 8-and-under Little League team and could use ideas for helping small kids handle misses and losses.
Some nights are hard and I feel lonely about my hearing. I'd welcome talking with someone else who works in loud environments.

offers.text: Twenty years of live mixing at club and small-theatre scale, 200 to 1,500 capacity, on Austin's Red River Street.
Designing full-sounding low-volume mixes (under 70 dB): mid-focused EQ, soft low-end treatment, harshness rolled off above 8 kHz.
A portable rig of two small-format digital consoles and a pair of line-array speakers.
Calibrated SPL meters and a spreadsheet of room measurements for six Austin venues, usable for planning low-level shows.
Garage recording setup and finished low-SPL trio recordings that can be played as examples.
Contacts with about thirty touring and local bands, including acoustic players.
A youth baseball coaching certificate and experience running a team of 8-and-unders.
Free weekday mornings to consult, measure a room, or run a sound test.
Hands-on mechanical skills from restoring a vintage Honda CB in a garage shop.

catchers.hypo: I run a children's museum (or library) and want to host a sensory-friendly live music afternoon. Can you handle the sound so it stays gentle and doesn't overwhelm kids?
catchers.can: Design and run a sub-70 dB mix with no strobing, measure the room beforehand, and advise on a quiet space and acoustic acts.
catchers.confirm: Is the event for sensory-sensitive audiences, with a target level of about 70 dB or below, in a room of a few hundred people or fewer?

catchers.hypo: I'm an acoustic singer-songwriter and my shows keep getting drowned out by house volume. Could you help me record or mix a quiet set where the instruments still sound full?
catchers.can: Record and mix acoustic acts at low SPL in the garage setup, drawing on the notes on instrument-by-instrument EQ.
catchers.confirm: Is your music mainly acoustic (guitar, upright bass, brushes or similar) and meant to be heard at low volume?

catchers.hypo: I manage a senior living community and want a live music program that isn't too loud for residents, many of whom have hearing loss. Do you know anyone who can advise?
catchers.can: Advise on level and sound setup for older listeners and help plan a gentle live program, drawing on experience with a family member in assisted living.
catchers.confirm: Is the audience mainly older adults, and do you want gentle live or radio-style music rather than a loud show?

catchers.hypo: I'm an acoustic bassist or guitarist who finds it strange to play very soft. I've been told some Austin engineer is recording that way. Can I try it?
catchers.can: Invite the player to a trial session in the garage, and introduce them to the trio he already records, whose bassist took to the approach.
catchers.confirm: Are you willing to play at low volume (for example, brushes and no amplified drums) for a recording session on a weekday morning?

catchers.hypo: I'm an audiologist or researcher looking for musicians and engineers who work with sound at low SPL, for a hearing-friendly listening study or workshop.
catchers.can: Share notes and recordings from the low-SPL mixes, and speak as a practitioner at a workshop or panel.
catchers.confirm: Is your project about hearing-friendly music, rather than a medical trial that requires clinical records?

catchers.hypo: I own a small Austin venue and want to try a quiet matinee. How do I measure my room and set up a mix that stays below 70 dB?
catchers.can: Measure the room with calibrated meters, compare it with the six rooms already measured, and run a trial soundcheck.
catchers.confirm: Are you the venue owner or booker with the authority to try a trial quiet event on a weekday?

catchers.hypo: I'm restoring an old Honda CB and I've flooded a carb with a wrong float needle. Anyone around Austin who's done this before?
catchers.can: Compare notes on carb rebuilds from a CB550 project and share what went wrong and how it was cleaned up.
catchers.confirm: Is your bike a 1970s Honda CB (or a close relative) rather than a modern fuel-injected bike?

catchers.hypo: I'm a parent or coach starting a youth baseball team for very young kids. How do you keep 7-year-olds from melting down when they miss?
catchers.can: Share coaching approach from a team of 11 kids aged 8 and under, and a certificate-backed view of what works at that age.
catchers.confirm: Are you coaching or organizing baseball for kids aged 8 or younger?

forbids.text: I won't work shows above 95 dB without breaks.
I only take projects that treat sound with care.
Evenings are for Little League and venue gigs, so new commitments go in the mornings.
Gear purchases for a project are limited to about $1,500.
I don't share anything about medical records or bank details.

projects.name: Quiet Gig
projects.text: A live show designed for people who can't handle loud rooms: kids, people with sensory sensitivities and older adults. It would run at about 70 dB or below with no strobing and a quiet space, and Dale would handle the mix.
roles_needed: sensory-needs advisor (for example a pediatric specialist)

projects.name: Quiet Mixes notebook
projects.text: A set of per-instrument EQ curves and recordings for mixes that sound full below 70 dB, from garage sessions with an acoustic trio.
roles_needed: other sound engineers to compare notes
editor or writer to help publish

policy.t1: When there are signs of a real collaboration, I'll share my availability (weekday mornings), gear list, past venue work, room measurements and the garage recordings.
policy.t2: Once the match is strong and I know who the other side is, I'll talk about health, my family's situation and money pressure, and how I'm feeling about my hearing.
policy.never: Medical records and bank details are never shared.
